title: Implementing low-carbon operations, waste separation, and student-led green audits in Hong Kong secondary schools
topic_description: Hong Kong secondary schools are expanding low-carbon operations, waste separation, and transparent reporting. Your Student Environmental Committee must debate whether green audits should be compulsory for senior forms, how poorer schools can meet goals fairly, and how to communicate with parents worried about HKDSE time loss.
instructions: You have 1 minute to prepare and 8 minutes for the group discussion (10 minutes for a group of 4). You should interact with your fellow candidates. Do not read out prepared notes. You may make notes during the preparation time, but you should not write out everything you plan to say.
discussion_points: Whether student-led green audits should be mandatory for Forms 4–6 and how workload can be managed without harming HKDSE preparation.
Equity between well-resourced and less-resourced schools when implementing sustainability targets and public dashboards.
Communication strategies for parents and alumni—transparency, data literacy, and realistic timelines.
individual_response_questions: To what extent should the government subsidise school retrofits instead of relying on PTAs and alumni donations?
How can English classrooms support sustainability literacy while maintaining the rigour expected in Paper 1 and Paper 2?
hkeaa_alignment: English Language Paper 4: Communication Skills (ideas/discourse/strategies), Language (range, accuracy), and delivery (naturalness, intelligibility) in the public examination framework.
success_feedback: You engaged with policy-education crossover issues at discussion depth appropriate to Level 5 expectations.
suggested_next_steps: Record a 60-second individual response; transcribe one improvement for lexical precision.
List five interactional moves (agree, hedge, redirect) used in your discussion.
